part.text: I identified the remaining nested dispatch bug: range elements were deliberately routed back through the string mapper. I’m adding a range-preserving overload ahead of generic mapping, while retaining the existing path-like exclusion.

   using mapper = arg_mapper<Context>;
 
+  template <typename T,
+            FMT_ENABLE_IF(is_range<remove_cvref_t<T>,
+                                  typename Context::char_type>::value)>
+  static auto map(T&& value) -> T&& {
+    return static_cast<T&&>(value);

   template <typename T,
-            FMT_ENABLE_IF(has_formatter<remove_cvref_t<T>, Context>::value)>
+            FMT_ENABLE_IF(!is_range<remove_cvref_t<T>,
+                                    typename Context::char_type>::value &&
+                          has_formatter<remove_cvref_t<T>, Context>::value)>
@@
   template <typename T,
-            FMT_ENABLE_IF(!has_formatter<remove_cvref_t<T>, Context>::value)>
+            FMT_ENABLE_IF(!is_range<remove_cvref_t<T>,

+                          !has_formatter<remove_cvref_t<T>, Context>::value)>

part.text:
Implemented the range formatting fix.

- Prevented C++23 `std::string_view` range construction from classifying arbitrary character ranges as strings.
- Corrected argument mapper constraints to check conversion from `const T&`, matching the value actually mapped.
- Bound mapped range elements before formatting, allowing transformed prvalue subranges such as the reported `X` example to compile.

Validation:
- The direct C++20 compile probe for the reported `X` transform-range case now succeeds.
- `cmake --build build --target ranges-test -j2` succeeds.
- Note: the existing `ranges-test` binary has one pre-existing injected-baseline failure in `ranges_test.format_vector`, which reproduces independently in this C++11-configured build.
